Gold: 1 = 100 crowns. deadline: seasons the King has to answer a card from its rider's arrival (a card's own deadline overrides), then it lapses and doing nothing costs. rider.speed: tiles a season the rider rides from the card's town to the King's seat (the card is seen coming, riding, and not answered until he arrives).

cards.subject: crown_town
cards.title: Rats in {town}'s granary
cards.text: The reeve of {town} brings a sack gnawed through. Half the winter's grain is fouled, and the town knows it.

text: Grain carts reach {town} before the rumour does.
The grain reaches {town} a day ahead of the gossip.

choices.label: Ration it, and say so

{town} eats less, knows why, and complains anyway.

A new mill goes up above the flood line.
The mill is rebuilt, higher on the bank.
The next flood passes {town}'s mill by; the miller blesses the King's foresight.
The next flood misses {town}'s mill, and the miller blesses the King.
The water rises and passes {town}'s mill; the miller praises the King's foresight.

choices.label: Grind by hand till summer
text: {town} grinds by hand, and its bread is coarse.
{town} grinds by hand, and eats coarse bread.
The bread of {town} is rough from the hand-querns.
{town} buys flour from upriver at a robber's price.
{town} pays a robber's price for flour from upriver.
Flour comes down to {town} from upriver, dearly bought.

cards.subject: crown_town
cards.title: Fire in {town}'s poor quarter
cards.text: A lamp tipped over and half a street of {town} burned. Families bed down in the square.

choices.label: Rebuild the street
text: Timber carts roll into {town} under the crown's mark.
Carts of timber bearing the crown's mark enter {town}.
The crown sends timber to {town}.

choices.label: Open the royal stores to them
text: The burned-out of {town} eat the King's bread this season.
This season, {town}'s burned-out eat the King's bread.
The royal stores feed {town}'s homeless for the season.

choices.label: They will build again; they always do
text: {town}'s poor rebuild with what they can scavenge.
{town}'s poor build again with whatever they can find.
The burned of {town} scavenge and rebuild.
The rebuilt street in {town} is tinder again; folk say the next fire is the King's.
{town}'s new street is tinder again; folk say the next fire belongs to the King.
The rebuilt street in {town} would burn at a spark, and they will blame the crown.
{town}'s homeless crowd the roads to Kingsmere.
The roads to Kingsmere fill with {town}'s homeless.
{town}'s burned-out walk to Kingsmere.

cards.subject: crown_town
cards.title: {town} accuses a widow of witchcraft
cards.text: A herb-woman of {town} is blamed for a dead calf and a stillborn child. The crowd has a rope.

choices.label: Spare her, and say why
text: The King's word stops the rope; some in {town} mutter.
The King stops the rope; some in {town} grumble.
By the King's word the widow lives, and {town} mutters.
The widow's herbs save a child in {town}; the town's tongue turns.
The widow's herbs save a child in {town}, and {town} changes its tune.
A child of {town} lives by the widow's herbs; the talk turns.

choices.label: Let the priests try her
text: The temple of {town} sits in judgement.
The temple of {town} sits to judge her.
In {town}, the priests try the widow.

choices.label: Give the crowd what it wants
text: The rope is used in {town}'s square.
The rope is put to use in {town}'s square.
{town}'s square gets its hanging.
{town} hangs her without the King's leave.
{town} hangs her, without leave from the King.
The widow hangs in {town}; nobody asked the King.

cards.subject: crown_town
cards.title: Bandits on the {town} road
cards.text: Merchants will not travel to {town} without a guard. The outlaws hide in the old forest.

choices.label: Clear the forest with soldiers
text: The King's men beat the forest for a week.
For a week, the King's men comb the forest.
Royal soldiers beat through the woods for a week.
The {town} road is safe again; carts come back.
The road to {town} is safe, and the carts return.
Carts come back to the {town} road now it is safe.

choices.label: Pardon any who lay down their bows
text: Some outlaws come in for the pardon; some laugh at it.
Some outlaws take the pardon; others laugh at it.
The pardon brings some outlaws in, and some to laughter.
Pardoned outlaws keep the {town} road for the King now.
The {town} road is now kept for the King by pardoned outlaws.
The outlaws who took the pardon now guard the {town} road.

choices.label: Let the merchants hire guards
text: The merchants hire guards, and add the cost to their prices.
The merchants pay for guards, and pass the cost on.
Guards are hired by the merchants, and prices rise to pay them.
Trade with {town} dries up; the outlaws grow fat.
Trade with {town} dries up, and the outlaws fatten.
The outlaws prosper; {town} sees fewer carts.

cards.subject: seat
cards.title: Beggars at the gates of {town}
cards.text: The roads have brought every hungry man in the realm to the King's own gate. The guards ask what to do.

choices.label: Feed them at the gate
text: Soup kettles steam at {town}'s gate every morning.
Every morning, soup steams at {town}'s gate.
The kettles at {town}'s gate feed the beggars each day.

choices.label: Put them to work on the walls
text: The beggars haul stone for bread.
The beggars carry stone in exchange for bread.
Bread is earned by hauling stone for the walls.
The beggars' wall stands; some stayed on as masons.
The wall the beggars built still stands; a few stayed as masons.
The beggars' wall is finished, and some of them are masons now.

choices.label: Drive them from the gate
text: The guards clear the gate with staves.
Guards with staves sweep the gate clear.
The beggars are driven off with staves.
The beggars camp at the gate; the lords step over them.
The beggars camp by the gate, and the lords step around them.
Lords pick their way over the beggars at the gate.

cards.subject: seat
cards.title: The court fool mocks the Hand
cards.text: At supper the fool aped the Hand's walk so well that the hall roared. The Hand did not.

choices.label: Reward the fool
text: The fool gets a silver bell. The Hand gets a sour look.
The fool receives a silver bell; the Hand receives a sour look.
A silver bell for the fool, and a scowl for the Hand.

choices.label: Make the fool apologise
text: The fool apologises in rhyme, which is worse.
The fool says sorry in verse, which is worse.
The apology comes rhymed, and stings more.
The rhyme has reached every tavern in {town}.
Every tavern in {town} knows the rhyme now.
{town}'s taverns are all singing the fool's rhyme.

choices.label: Whip the fool
text: The hall goes quiet when the fool is led out.
When the fool is taken out, the hall falls silent.
A hush falls as the fool is led away.
The fool does it again the next night, to more laughter.
The next night the fool does it again, and gets more laughs.
The fool repeats it the following night, to a louder hall.

cards.subject: seat
cards.title: The priests want a greater temple
cards.text: The high priest says {town}'s temple is too small for a king's prayers. He has drawings.

choices.label: Build it, whatever it costs
text: Masons from three realms come to {town}.
{town} fills with masons from three realms.
Three realms send their masons to {town}.
The great temple of {town} is hallowed; lords come from every house to see it.
{town}'s great temple is hallowed, and every house sends lords to see it.
Lords of every house come to see the new temple of {town} blessed.

choices.label: A new roof will do
text: The old temple gets a new lead roof.
The old temple is given a fresh roof of lead.
New lead goes on the old temple's roof.

choices.label: The gods hear prayers in small rooms too
text: The high priest rolls up his drawings, slowly.
The high priest slowly rolls up his plans.
The drawings are rolled away, slowly, by the high priest.
The high priest preaches on kings who forget the gods.
The high priest preaches on kings who neglect the gods.
From the pulpit, the high priest speaks of kings forgetful of heaven.

cards.subject: seat
cards.title: Clipped coin in the treasury
cards.text: The master of the mint shows the King a fistful of crowns, every one shaved at the rim.

choices.label: Recoin the whole treasury
text: The mint runs day and night to strike honest coin.
Day and night the mint strikes honest coin.
The mint never sleeps, striking coin of true weight.
Merchants trust the crown's coin again; the tolls come in full.
The merchants trust the crown's coin again, and the tolls come in whole.
Honest coin brings the merchants back, and the tolls in full.

choices.label: Hang the clippers when found
text: Gibbets go up by {town}'s mint.
Gibbets rise beside {town}'s mint.
By the mint in {town}, gibbets are raised.

choices.label: Shave the next coinage too
text: The crown's coin goes out lighter, and the crown a little richer.
The coin goes out lighter, and the crown somewhat richer.
Lighter coin leaves the mint; the crown keeps the difference.
Foreign merchants weigh the King's coin and laugh.
Foreign merchants put the King's coin on the scales and laugh.
The King's coin is weighed abroad, and mocked.
Clipped coin passes through every market in the realm.
Every market in the realm takes clipped coin.
Shaved coin goes from hand to hand across the realm.

cards.subject: realm
cards.title: Pilgrims crowd the roads
cards.text: A holy year brings pilgrims to every shrine. Innkeepers grow rich; constables grow tired.

choices.label: Build hostels on the pilgrim roads
text: Hostels with the crown's sign go up along the roads.
Hostels bearing the crown's sign rise along the roads.
The pilgrim roads gain hostels under the royal sign.
Pilgrims pray for the King in every hostel he built.
In every hostel he built, pilgrims pray for the King.
The King's hostels fill with pilgrims praying for him.

choices.label: Toll the pilgrims
text: Every pilgrim pays a penny at the crown's bridges.
At the crown's bridges, each pilgrim pays a penny.
A penny a head goes to the crown at every bridge.

choices.label: Let them pass as they will
text: The roads fill, and empty, as they always have.
The roads fill and empty, as ever.
Pilgrims come and go as they always have.
A pilgrim crush at a ford drowns a dozen; the priests ask where the King was.
A dozen pilgrims drown in a crush at a ford, and the priests ask where the King was.
At a crowded ford a dozen drown; the priests wonder aloud where the crown stood.

cards.subject: realm
cards.title: A comet over the realm
cards.text: A tailed star hangs in the night sky. The priests say it means a king's death; the astrologers, a king's triumph.

choices.label: Pay the astrologers to proclaim it
text: Criers read the astrologers' happy reading in every town.
In every town, criers announce the astrologers' cheerful verdict.
The happy reading is cried in every town at the King's expense.

choices.label: Hold a great sacrifice
text: Oxen burn at every temple in the King's name.
Oxen are burned in the King's name at every temple.
Every temple burns oxen for the King.

choices.label: It is a star, and nothing more
text: Some lords think the King brave; more think him rash.
A few lords call the King brave; more call him reckless.
Some think him bold for it, and more think him rash.
The comet fades and the King still lives; the doubters go quiet.
The comet goes, the King lives, and the doubters hush.
The King outlasts the comet; the doubters fall silent.
Every lord reads the comet his own way.
Each lord reads the comet to suit himself.
The lords all find their own meaning in the comet.

cards.subject: realm
cards.title: A foreign queen sends gifts
cards.text: Across the sea a queen sends silks and a white horse, and asks nothing yet.

choices.label: Send richer gifts back
text: Gold and a falcon sail to the queen.
A falcon and gold are shipped to the queen.
The queen is sent gold and a falcon.
The foreign queen's ships trade freely in the King's ports.
The foreign queen's ships trade freely in the King's harbours.
The King's ports open freely to the queen's ships.

choices.label: A courteous letter
text: A letter goes back, warm and empty.
A letter goes back, kind and hollow.
The queen gets a warm letter with nothing in it.

choices.label: Keep the horse and say nothing
text: The queen hears nothing, and remembers it.
The queen hears nothing, and does not forget.
No word reaches the queen; she remembers.
The foreign queen's ships tax the King's merchants.
The foreign queen's ships levy tax on the King's merchants.
The King's merchants pay dues to the queen's ships.
The white horse grazes at Kingsmere; the queen waits for a word.
The white horse grazes at Kingsmere, and the queen waits for word.
At Kingsmere, the white horse eats; abroad, the queen waits.

cards.subject: realm
cards.title: Salt is dear this year
cards.text: The salt pans flooded and the price has tripled. No salt, no salted meat for winter.

choices.label: Buy salt for the realm
text: Salt carts carry the crown's barrels to every town.
The crown's salt goes by cart to every town.
Every town gets salt barrels bearing the crown's mark.

choices.label: Fix the price by decree
text: Salt is sold at the King's price, where it is sold at all.
Salt sells at the King's price, wherever any is sold.
Where salt can be had, it costs what the King says.
Salt merchants hide their stock; the markets go short.
The salt merchants hide their stocks, and the markets go without.
Salt vanishes into merchants' cellars; the markets run short.

choices.label: Tax the salt merchants' windfall
text: The crown takes its share of the dear salt.
The crown takes its cut of the dear salt.
Of the high price of salt, the crown claims a share.
Winter comes on unsalted meat; the realm eats poorly.
Winter comes and the meat is unsalted; the realm eats badly.
Unsalted meat greets the winter, and the realm eats poorly.

cards.subject: realm
cards.title: The steward wants a count of the realm
cards.text: Every hearth, every plough, every head of cattle. The steward says the crown is being cheated blind.

choices.label: Count it all
text: The King's clerks ride out with ledgers.
The clerks ride out, ledgers in hand.
Out go the King's clerks with their ledgers.
The count is done; the tithe comes in fuller.
The count is finished, and the tithe comes in fuller.
With the count done, the tithe swells.

choices.label: Count the crown's own towns only
text: Clerks count the royal towns, which grumble alone.
Only the royal towns are counted, and they grumble alone.
The crown's own towns are counted, and complain by themselves.
The royal towns' count turns up hidden fields.
The royal towns' count finds fields no one had declared.
Hidden fields turn up in the royal towns' count.

choices.label: A count makes enemies
text: The steward closes his ledger, unhappily.
The steward shuts his ledger, displeased.
Unhappily, the steward closes the book.
The steward keeps guessing, and guessing low.
The steward goes on guessing, and guessing low.
The guesses continue, and they are low.

cards.subject: realm
cards.title: A ship of the dead in harbour
cards.text: A merchantman drifted in with its crew dead at the oars. The dockers will not touch it.

choices.label: Burn the ship where it lies
text: The ship burns in the harbour mouth, its cargo with it.
The ship and its cargo burn at the harbour mouth.
At the harbour mouth, the ship goes up with all it carried.
Whatever killed that crew came no further.
Whatever took that crew got no further.
The thing that killed the crew went no further.

choices.label: Salvage the cargo first
text: The crown's men unload spices and silk, wrapped in cloth.
Wrapped in cloth, spices and silk come ashore in the crown's hands.
The crown's men bring off the silk and spices, cloth-wrapped.
A fever runs along the docks.
Fever spreads along the docks.
The docks take a fever.

choices.label: Tow it out to sea
text: The ship drifts away on the tide, somewhere else's trouble.
The tide takes the ship away, to be someone else's problem.
Towed out, the ship drifts off to trouble another shore.
Thieves strip the ship by night.
Thieves strip the ship in the night.
By night, the ship is picked clean by thieves.

cards.subject: crown_town
cards.title: A chain across the river below {town}
cards.text: Someone has strung a chain across the river and charges every barge. {town}'s trade chokes.

choices.label: Cut the chain
text: Royal men cut the chain at dawn.
At dawn, royal men cut the chain.
The chain is cut by the King's men at first light.

choices.label: Buy out the toll
text: The crown pays the chain's owner to take it down.
The crown pays the owner to take the chain down.
The chain comes down, bought out by the crown.

choices.label: Put the crown's own toll there
text: The chain stays; the King's men collect.
The chain remains, and the King's men take the toll.
Nothing moves but the hands on the chain; the crown collects now.
{town}'s merchants move their trade to the road.
The merchants of {town} take their goods by road instead.
{town}'s trade leaves the river for the road.
{town}'s barges pay twice, and the town pays for it.
{town}'s barges pay two tolls, and the town bears the cost.
Every barge from {town} pays twice, and {town} feels it.

cards.subject: crown_town
cards.title: Gold in the hills by {town}
cards.text: A shepherd found yellow stones in a stream above {town}. Every chancer in the realm is on the road.

choices.label: Claim it for the crown
text: Royal miners stake the hill above {town}.
The crown's miners mark out the hill above {town}.
Above {town}, royal miners claim the hill.
The mine above {town} sends its first chest to Kingsmere.
The first chest from the mine above {town} reaches Kingsmere.
Kingsmere receives the first gold from the hill above {town}.

choices.label: Let anyone dig and tax the finds
text: {town} fills with diggers and quarrels.
{town} is overrun with diggers and their quarrels.
Diggers crowd into {town}, and the quarrelling starts.

choices.label: Reward the shepherd and seal it
text: The shepherd gets a purse; the stream gets a guard.
A purse for the shepherd, and a guard on the stream.
The stream is guarded, and the shepherd paid.
Diggers tear up the hill and fight over it; the gold goes into their pockets.
The hill is torn apart by brawling diggers, and the gold stays in their pockets.
Diggers fight over the hill, and keep what they find.

cards.subject: realm
cards.title: Hail flattens the barley
cards.text: A summer storm laid the fields flat from the coast to the hills. The lords count their losses aloud.

choices.label: Forgive a season's tithe
text: The houses keep their tithe this season.
This season the houses keep their tithe.
No tithe is taken from the houses this season.

choices.label: Lend seed for a second sowing
text: Seed carts go out under the crown's mark.
Carts of seed bearing the crown's mark go out.
The crown sends seed for a second sowing.
A late harvest comes in thin but whole.
The late harvest is thin, but it is all brought in.
A thin crop comes in late, and nothing is lost.

choices.label: Every house bears its own luck
text: The lords bear it, and bear it in mind.
The lords endure it, and do not forget it.
Each house bears its loss, and remembers who let it.
The realm tightens its belt for winter.
The realm pulls its belt tight for the winter.
Winter will be lean across the realm.

cards.subject: seat
cards.title: The spring fair at {town}
cards.text: Players, jugglers and a dancing bear want a pitch at {town}'s fair. The King's own presence would be a wonder.

choices.label: Open the fair yourself
text: The King cuts the ribbon; the crowd cheers itself hoarse.
The King opens the fair, and the crowd cheers itself hoarse.
A royal hand cuts the ribbon; the crowd roars.

choices.label: Charge the players for their pitch
text: The fair pays the crown its share.
The crown takes its share from the fair.
Players pay for their pitches, and the crown is richer.

choices.label: No bears in the King's city
text: The bear goes back up the road, dancing.
The bear dances its way back up the road.
Out of the city goes the bear, still dancing.
The fair goes on, and nobody asks the King.
The fair carries on, and no one asks the King anything.
Nobody consults the King; the fair goes on regardless.

cards.subject: crown_town
cards.title: Midsummer fires at {town}
cards.text: The young of {town} want to leap the bonfires as their grandfathers did. The priests call it heathen.

choices.label: Light the fires, and join them
text: The King's health is drunk around {town}'s fires.
Around {town}'s fires, they drink to the King.
{town} toasts the crown by firelight.

choices.label: Side with the priests
text: The fires stay dark; the young sulk.
The fires stay unlit, and the young sulk.
No fires are lit; the young folk mope.

choices.label: Let the town decide
text: {town} decides, loudly, both ways.
{town} decides both ways, and loudly.
{town} argues it out and settles on both answers.
The fires burn without the King's blessing; the priests write to Kingsmere.
The fires burn unblessed, and the priests send letters to Kingsmere.
With no word from the King, the fires burn and the priests complain by post.

cards.subject: crown_town
cards.title: {town} asks the King to its harvest home
cards.text: The last sheaf is in. {town} would like the King at its table, or at least his wine.

choices.label: Send a cart of wine
text: {town} drinks to the King until the barrels are dry.
{town} toasts the King till the last barrel runs dry.
The wine lasts until {town} has drunk the King's health many times.

choices.label: Go in person
text: The King sits at {town}'s long table; they will talk of it for years.
The King takes a seat at {town}'s long table; it will be talked of for years.
{town} will speak for years of the King at its harvest table.
{town} still tells of the night the King came to harvest home.
{town} still talks of the King at its harvest home.
The night the King came to harvest home is still told in {town}.

choices.label: The King has his own harvest to count
text: {town} feasts without him.
{town} holds its feast without the King.
{town} feasts alone.
{town} feasts, and notes the empty chair.
{town} feasts, and sees the chair left empty.
The empty chair at {town}'s feast is noticed.

cards.subject: crown_town
cards.title: The river freezes at {town}
cards.text: Ice a hand thick from bank to bank. The boats are stuck, but a road has opened where none was.

choices.label: Run carts across the ice
text: Carts cross the river at {town} all winter.
All winter, carts cross the ice at {town}.
The frozen river at {town} carries carts until spring.
A cart went through the ice at {town}; the town mourns.
A cart broke through the ice at {town}, and {town} mourns.
{town} grieves a cart lost under the ice.

choices.label: Mark a safe crossing
text: The King's men stake a safe road across the ice.
The King's men stake out a safe way over the ice.
A safe crossing is marked across the ice by royal stakes.

choices.label: Forbid the ice
text: The ice stays empty; the boats wait for spring.
No one crosses the ice; the boats wait for spring.
The ice is left bare, and the boats wait.
Folk cross where they like, and some don't come back.
People cross wherever they please, and some never reach the far side.
Folk pick their own way over the ice; not all return.

cards.subject: seat
cards.title: The white stag
cards.text: The huntsmen have found a white stag in the royal forest. The lords want to ride with the King.

choices.label: Ride out with all the lords
text: Horns sound from the forest all day.
All day, horns ring from the forest.
The forest echoes with hunting horns from dawn to dusk.

choices.label: Hunt it alone
text: The King brings back the white stag himself.
The King brings home the white stag with his own hands.
Alone, the King returns with the white stag.
The white stag's antlers hang in the hall; the lords who weren't asked look at them.
The white stag's antlers hang in the hall, watched by the lords who were left behind.
Lords who were not invited stare at the antlers in the hall.

choices.label: Let the stag run
text: The stag stays in the forest; the huntsmen sigh.
The stag runs free in the forest, and the huntsmen sigh.
The huntsmen sigh as the stag is left to the woods.
A lord's son kills the white stag, and boasts.
A lord's son brings down the white stag, and brags of it.
The white stag falls to a lord's boastful son.

cards.subject: seat
cards.title: Old soldiers at the gate
cards.text: Men who bled for the King's father beg at the gate on crutches. They ask what was promised.

choices.label: Pensions for every one
text: The old soldiers draw their pay at Kingsmere.
The old soldiers collect their pay at Kingsmere.
Each veteran draws a pension at Kingsmere.
Old soldiers drill the young levy for the King, unasked.
Unbidden, old soldiers drill the young levy for the King.
The veterans train the King's new levy without being asked.

choices.label: A hall for them to live in
text: An old barracks becomes a home for the King's veterans.
The King's veterans make their home in an old barracks.
An old barracks is given over to the veterans.

choices.label: That was the old King's promise
text: The veterans go, cursing two kings now.
The veterans leave, now cursing two kings.
Off go the old soldiers, with a curse for each king.
The old soldiers die at the gate one by one; the guards stop counting.
One by one, the old soldiers die at the gate, and the guards no longer count them.
The guards have stopped counting the veterans dead at the gate.

cards.subject: crown_town
cards.title: Good stone near {town}
cards.text: Masons say the hill by {town} is fine pale stone, the kind temples are built of.

choices.label: Open a royal quarry
text: Quarrymen cut into the hill by {town}.
Quarrymen begin cutting the hill by {town}.
The hill at {town} is opened by royal quarrymen.
Pale stone from {town} sells across the realm.
{town}'s pale stone sells throughout the realm.
The realm buys the pale stone of {town}.

choices.label: Let {town} quarry it
text: {town} sells the stone and keeps the silver.
{town} quarries, sells the stone and keeps the silver.
The silver from the stone stays in {town}.

choices.label: Leave the hill be
text: The hill keeps its stone.
The stone stays in the hill.
No one cuts the hill.
A great house quarries it without asking.
A great house quarries it without leave.
Without asking, a great house starts cutting the stone.

cards.subject: realm
cards.title: The sun goes dark at noon
cards.text: For a quarter hour the sky went black. Cattle lay down; men knelt in the fields.

choices.label: Proclaim it a blessing on the King
text: The temples call it the gods' wink at their chosen king.
The temples call it the gods winking at the King they chose.
The priests proclaim the dark sun a wink from heaven to its chosen King.

choices.label: Fast and pray across the realm
text: A day of fasting is called; the realm prays with the King.
The realm fasts a day and prays alongside the King.
A fast is called, and the realm prays with its King.

choices.label: Let the priests sort it out
text: The priests sort it out, each his own way.
Each priest sorts it out in his own fashion.
The priests settle it, every one differently.
Prophets in every market say the King's days are numbered.
In every market, prophets say the King's days are counted.
Prophets cry in the markets that the King will not last.

cards.subject: realm
cards.title: A boy claims royal blood
cards.text: A beggar's boy in the north says he is the King's half-brother. He has a ring, and the old nurse backs him.

choices.label: Bring him to court and look at him
text: The boy comes to Kingsmere, wide-eyed.
The boy arrives at Kingsmere, staring at everything.
Kingsmere receives a wide-eyed boy.
The boy grows up at court, the King's man; the rumour dies with the nurse.
The boy grows up at court as the King's man, and the rumour is buried with the nurse.
Raised at court, the boy serves the King; the tale dies when the nurse does.

choices.label: Pay the nurse to recant
text: The nurse recants, richer.
The nurse takes it back, and the silver too.
Paid, the nurse unsays it.

choices.label: Have him taken quietly
text: The boy is not seen again.
No one sees the boy again.
The boy vanishes.
A lord says the boy was murdered by the crown.
A lord claims the crown had the boy killed.
The boy's murder is laid at the crown's door by a lord.
A great house takes the boy in, and feeds the rumour.
A great house shelters the boy and keeps the rumour fed.
The boy finds a home with a great house, and so does the rumour.

cards.subject: crown_town
cards.title: A monk of {town} copies books for coin
cards.text: A monk at {town} sells copied psalters to merchants. His abbot says it shames the order.

choices.label: Buy his books for the crown's library
text: The King's library grows by a shelf.
A new shelf is added to the King's library.
The crown's library gains a shelf of books.
Clerks taught from {town}'s books keep the King's accounts honest.
Clerks schooled on {town}'s books keep the King's accounts straight.
{town}'s books teach clerks who keep the crown's ledgers honest.

choices.label: Side with the abbot
text: The monk goes back to his prayers.
The monk returns to his prayers.
Back to prayer goes the monk.

choices.label: Let him sell, and tax it
text: The monk pays the crown's tithe on his ink.
The monk pays the crown a tithe on his ink.
The crown takes a tithe of the monk's sales.
The monk keeps copying, and the abbot keeps writing to Kingsmere.
The monk copies on, and the abbot keeps writing to Kingsmere.
Ink flows from the monk, and letters from the abbot.

cards.subject: crown_town
cards.title: Smugglers in {town}'s cove
cards.text: Wine and silk come ashore at night by {town}, and none of it pays duty.

choices.label: Set a watch on the cove
text: The King's men watch the cove all season.
All season, the King's men keep watch on the cove.
The cove is watched by royal men through the season.
The smugglers are caught with a full boat; the cargo is the crown's.
The smugglers are taken with a full boat, and the crown keeps the cargo.
A laden smugglers' boat is caught, and its goods go to the crown.

choices.label: Take a cut and look away
text: The smugglers pay the crown to keep its lanterns dark.
The crown is paid to keep its lanterns unlit.
The smugglers buy the crown's blind eye.

choices.label: Hang the first one you catch
text: A smuggler hangs at {town}'s quay.
At {town}'s quay, a smuggler hangs.
{town}'s quay gets a hanged smuggler.
{town}'s merchants buy from the cove and stop paying at the quay.
{town}'s merchants buy at the cove and pay nothing at the quay.
The quay at {town} goes unpaid while the merchants deal at the cove.

cards.subject: crown_town
cards.title: {town}'s tithe barn burns
cards.text: The barn that held the crown's share of {town}'s harvest went up in a night. Some say it was no accident.

choices.label: Find who lit it
text: The reeve's men question half of {town}.
Half of {town} is questioned by the reeve's men.
The reeve's men put questions to half of {town}.
It was the tithe-reeve himself, hiding his thefts.
The tithe-reeve lit it himself, to hide his stealing.
It was the tithe-reeve, covering his own thefts.

choices.label: Rebuild and say nothing
text: A new barn rises at {town}.
{town} gets a new barn.
{town} quietly gets a new barn.

choices.label: Make {town} pay the tithe again
text: {town} pays twice, and hates the crown for it.
{town} pays its tithe twice, and hates the crown for it.
Twice taxed, {town} curses the King.
{town} keeps its harvest this year, by fire.
The fire lets {town} keep its harvest this year.
This year {town}'s harvest stays in {town}, thanks to the flames.

cards.subject: house_warm
cards.title: {lord} offers a daughter's hand
cards.text: {lord} of {house} would wed a daughter to the King's nephew. A bond of blood, and a claim with it.

choices.label: Accept the match
text: Bells ring at {town} for the betrothal.
{town} rings its bells for the betrothal.
The betrothal is rung in at {town}.
A child of both houses is born; {house} is the crown's kin now.
A child of both houses is born, and {house} is kin to the crown now.
With a child born to both lines, {house} joins the crown's family.

choices.label: Ask for a richer dowry
text: {lord} haggles, and pays.
{lord} bargains, then pays.
{lord} haggles; {lord} pays.

choices.label: Decline with honour
text: {lord} takes the refusal politely, and coldly.
{lord} accepts the refusal, courteous and cold.
The refusal is taken by {lord} politely, without warmth.
{lord} weds the daughter elsewhere.
{lord} marries the daughter off elsewhere.
The daughter of {lord} weds into another house.

cards.subject: house_cold
cards.title: {house}'s tribute is late again
cards.text: Two seasons now {house} has sent excuses instead of silver. {lord} pleads poor harvests at {town}.

choices.label: Send collectors with spears
text: Royal spears ride into {town} to count {house}'s silver.
The crown's spears enter {town} to count the silver of {house}.
Spearmen ride into {town} to reckon {house}'s silver.
{house} pays on time now, and hates every coin of it.
{house} is punctual now, and loathes each coin it pays.
The tribute of {house} arrives on time, and resentful.

choices.label: Forgive it this once
text: {lord} thanks the King, and wonders how far it goes.
{lord} thanks the King, and wonders how much else will be forgiven.
Grateful, {lord} wonders where the King's patience ends.
{house}'s tribute is late again.
Once more, {house} is late with its tribute.
The tribute of {house} is overdue again.

choices.label: Take a hostage instead
text: {house}'s heir comes to court as the King's guest.
The heir of {house} arrives at court, a guest of the King.
{house} sends its heir to Kingsmere to stay.
The heir of {house} grows fond of Kingsmere.
{house}'s heir grows to like Kingsmere.
Kingsmere wins the fondness of the heir of {house}.
Other houses note that {house} pays nothing, and wonder why they do.
The other houses see that {house} pays nothing, and ask why they should.
{house} pays nothing, and the other houses begin to wonder at paying.

cards.subject: house_any
cards.title: An heir is born to {house}
cards.text: {lord}'s wife has borne a son at {town}. The bells have rung there for a day and a night.

choices.label: Send a golden cup
text: A gold cup with the crown's mark goes to {town}.
A golden cup bearing the crown's mark is sent to {town}.
{town} receives a gold cup marked with the crown.

choices.label: Stand as the child's godfather
text: The King's name is spoken over the font at {town}.
At {town}'s font, the King's name is spoken.
The King's name is said over the child at {town}.
{house}'s heir, the King's godson, rides to court sworn to him.
The King's godson, heir of {house}, comes to court sworn to him.
The heir of {house} rides to court, sworn to the King who stood godfather.

choices.label: A letter of good wishes
text: A letter goes to {town}.
{town} receives a letter.
A letter of good wishes goes to {town}.
{lord} counts the gifts and finds none from Kingsmere.
{lord} counts the gifts; none came from Kingsmere.
Among the gifts, {lord} finds nothing from the King.

cards.subject: house_any
cards.title: {lord} lies dying
cards.text: {lord} of {house} has taken to bed and will not rise. The question is who rules {town} after.

choices.label: Back the eldest son
text: The King's word goes to the eldest; {house} is settled.
The King backs the eldest, and {house} is settled.
{house} is settled on the eldest son, by the King's word.

choices.label: Back the clever daughter
text: The daughter rules {house} by the King's leave; the son sulks.
By the King's leave the daughter rules {house}, and the son sulks.
The son sulks while the daughter takes {house}, with the crown behind her.
The daughter of {house} rules well, and remembers who backed her.
{house}'s daughter rules well, and does not forget who backed her.
The daughter governs {house} ably, and remembers the King's support.

choices.label: Let {house} sort it out
text: {house} argues over the deathbed.
{house} quarrels at the deathbed.
The deathbed of {house} becomes a quarrel.
{house} splits over the succession; brothers glare across {town}'s hall.
{house} divides over the succession; brothers scowl across {town}'s hall.
Brothers glower at each other in {town}'s hall as {house} splits.

cards.subject: house_warm
cards.title: {lord} wants a grander title
cards.text: {lord} of {house} has served well and would be called Duke. It costs the crown nothing but pride.

choices.label: Make {lord} a Duke
text: Heralds proclaim the Duke of {town}.
The heralds cry out the Duke of {town}.
{town} gets a Duke, by herald's cry.

choices.label: A title for the heir, later
text: {lord} is promised; {lord} waits.
{lord} gets a promise, and waits on it.
A promise is made; {lord} waits.
{lord} asks again about the promised title.
{lord} asks once more about the promised title.
The promised title comes up again from {lord}.

choices.label: Titles are earned on the field
text: {lord} goes home to earn it.
{lord} rides home to earn the title.
Home goes {lord}, to win it in the field.
{lord} styles themself Duke anyway, in letters.
In letters, {lord} signs as Duke regardless.
{lord} takes the title on paper, unasked.

cards.subject: house_any
cards.title: {house} is drowning in debt
cards.text: {lord} owes moneylenders more than {town} earns in five years. They ask the crown to stand surety.

choices.label: Pay the debt outright
text: {house}'s debt is the crown's now, and paid.
The crown takes on {house}'s debt, and pays it.
{house} owes nothing now; the crown has paid.

choices.label: Lend at fair interest
text: The crown becomes {house}'s banker.
{house} now banks with the crown.
The crown lends to {house}, at a fair rate.
{house} repays the crown's loan with interest.
{house} pays back the crown's loan, with interest.
The loan returns from {house}, interest and all.

choices.label: {house} made its bed
text: The moneylenders move into {town}.
{town} gets the moneylenders.
The moneylenders settle into {town}.
The moneylenders seize {house}'s mills at {town}.
{house}'s mills at {town} are taken by the moneylenders.
The moneylenders claim the mills of {house} at {town}.

cards.subject: house_any
cards.title: {lord} wants a better seat at table
cards.text: {lord} of {house} is tired of sitting below the salt. Someone must move down for {lord} to move up.

choices.label: Raise {lord} up
text: {lord} sits nearer the King; another lord sits further off.
{lord} moves closer to the King; another lord moves further away.
One lord rises toward the King's chair, and {lord} is the one; another drops back.

choices.label: Seat the lords by lot
text: Every feast the seats are drawn by lot. Everyone is equally annoyed.
Seats at every feast are drawn by lot, and all are equally put out.
Lots decide the seating now; nobody is pleased, fairly.

choices.label: The seats stay as they are
text: {lord} sits below the salt and chews hard.
{lord} sits below the salt, chewing hard.
Below the salt, {lord} chews in silence.
{lord} stops coming to feasts.
{lord} no longer comes to feasts.
The feasts go on without {lord}.

cards.subject: house_cold
cards.title: {house} builds a fort facing Kingsmere
cards.text: New walls rise on {house}'s side of the river, and their arrow slits look toward the crown's lands.

choices.label: Order it torn down
text: The King's order is read at {town}'s gate.
The King's order is read aloud at {town}'s gate.
At the gate of {town}, the order is proclaimed.
{house} pulls the fort down stone by stone, slowly.
Stone by stone, and slowly, {house} takes the fort down.
{house} dismantles the fort, in no hurry.

choices.label: Build one facing back
text: The crown's masons answer stone with stone.
The crown's masons build stone against stone.
A royal fort rises facing the other.

choices.label: Ask {lord} why, kindly
text: {lord} says it faces the wolves, not the King.
{lord} says the fort watches for wolves, not the King.
According to {lord}, it is wolves the fort faces.
The fort facing Kingsmere is manned now.
The fort that faces Kingsmere now has a garrison.
Men now stand in the fort that looks toward Kingsmere.
The fort is finished, and filled with spears.
The fort is completed and full of spears.
Spears fill the finished fort.

cards.subject: house_warm
cards.title: {lord} offers the crown a loan
cards.text: {house} has silver to spare and loyalty to show. {lord} would lend the crown a chest, at a kind rate.

choices.label: Take the loan
text: {house}'s silver comes to Kingsmere.
The silver of {house} arrives at Kingsmere.
Kingsmere takes {house}'s silver.
{house} asks for its silver back, with interest.
{house} wants its silver back, interest included.
The loan is called in by {house}, with interest.

choices.label: Ask a gift, not a loan
text: {lord} gives, with a smile that slips.
{lord} gives it, with a smile that does not quite hold.
The gift comes from {lord}, the smile slipping.

choices.label: The crown needs no lender
text: {lord} keeps the silver, and the offer stands.
{lord} keeps the silver, and the offer stays open.
The silver stays with {lord}, still on offer.
{lord} lends it to a rival house instead.
{lord} lends to a rival house instead.
A rival house gets the loan from {lord}.

cards.subject: house_cold
cards.title: {lord} refuses to come to court
cards.text: Summoned three times, {lord} of {house} sends only letters. They say {lord} fears the King's justice.

choices.label: Promise safe conduct
text: {lord} comes to Kingsmere under the King's word.
On the King's word, {lord} comes to Kingsmere.
{lord} arrives at Kingsmere under safe conduct.
{lord} kneels at court, and the realm sees the King's word kept.
{lord} kneels at court, and the realm sees the King kept his word.
The realm watches {lord} kneel, and the King's word hold.

choices.label: Declare {lord} outlaw
text: {lord}'s name is read out at every market cross.
At every market cross, {lord}'s name is cried out.
{lord} is named outlaw at each market cross.

choices.label: Send a fourth summons
text: The fourth letter goes to {town}.
A fourth letter is sent to {town}.
{town} receives the fourth summons.
{house} rules {town} as if there were no King.
{house} governs {town} as though the King did not exist.
In {town}, {house} rules with no thought of the crown.

cards.subject: house_any
cards.title: {lord} sends a sick horse as a gift
cards.text: {house} sent the King a horse that coughed itself dead in the royal stable. The grooms say it was ill when it came.

choices.label: Take it as an insult
text: {lord} hears the King's anger, and protests their innocence.
{lord} hears of the King's anger and swears innocence.
Faced with the King's anger, {lord} protests.

choices.label: Send a sick horse back
text: A coughing nag arrives at {town}; {house} gets the joke, or doesn't.
A wheezing nag reaches {town}; {house} may or may not see the joke.
{town} receives a coughing horse, and {house} is left to puzzle at it.
{lord} laughs about the horse at court; the two of you are easier.
{lord} jokes about the horse at court, and things between you ease.
The horse becomes a jest for {lord} at court; relations warm.

choices.label: Say nothing
text: The grooms bury the horse.
The horse is buried by the grooms.
The grooms dig a grave for the horse.
The grooms gossip; the court hears that {house} sent the King a dead horse.
The grooms talk, and the court learns {house} sent the King a dead horse.
Word spreads from the stables: {house} gave the King a dying horse.

cards.subject: house_any
cards.title: {lord}'s bastard asks for a name
cards.text: A bastard of {house} has fought well under the King's banner and asks to bear the house's name.

choices.label: Legitimise them
text: The King's seal makes a new heir of {house}.
The King's seal gives {house} a new heir.
{house} has a new heir by royal seal.
The legitimised bastard of {house} is the King's most loyal sword.
{house}'s legitimised bastard is the King's most loyal blade.
No sword serves the King more loyally than the bastard of {house}.

choices.label: Knight them instead
text: A new knight kneels before the King, nameless but honoured.
A new knight kneels to the King, honoured though nameless.
The bastard is knighted, without a name but with honour.

choices.label: A bastard is a bastard
text: They go back to the ranks.
Back to the ranks they go.
They return to the ranks.
The bastard joins a rival's household.
The bastard enters a rival's service.
A rival takes the bastard into his household.

cards.subject: war_pair
cards.title: {house} asks the King to judge its war
cards.text: {lord} of {house} comes to Kingsmere with a list of {rival}'s crimes, and asks the King to name the guilty.

choices.label: Name {rival} guilty
text: The crown's judgement goes against {rival}.
The crown finds against {rival}.
{rival} is judged guilty by the crown.

choices.label: Name both guilty
text: Both houses are fined for breaking the King's peace.
Each house is fined for breaking the peace.
The King fines both houses alike.

choices.label: Hear {rival}'s side first
text: Heralds ride to {rival} for its account.
Heralds go to {rival} to hear its account.
{rival} is asked for its side by royal heralds.
Both houses have stated their case; the court is tired of it.
Both houses have had their say, and the court is weary of it.
The court has heard both houses out, and is tired.
{house} decides the King has no judgement to give.
{house} concludes the King has no judgement to offer.
{house} decides the crown will not judge.

cards.subject: war_pair
cards.title: {rival} holds {house}'s knights
cards.text: A dozen knights of {house} sit in {rival}'s cells. {lord} begs the King to buy them out.

choices.label: Pay the ransom
text: The knights ride home to {town} on the crown's silver.
The crown's silver brings the knights home to {town}.
The knights return to {town}, ransomed by the King.

choices.label: Order {rival} to free them
text: The King's order goes to {rival}.
{rival} receives the King's order.
The order goes out to {rival}.
{rival} frees half the knights, and keeps the rich ones.
{rival} lets half the knights go, keeping the wealthy ones.
Half the knights come home; {rival} holds the rich.

choices.label: A war's prisoners are a war's business
text: {lord} goes home empty-handed.
{lord} rides home with nothing.
Empty-handed, {lord} leaves.
{house}'s knights rot in {rival}'s cells.
The knights of {house} waste away in {rival}'s cells.
{rival}'s cells hold {house}'s knights, rotting.

cards.subject: war_pair
cards.title: {house} and {rival} fight over a ford
cards.text: One crossing on the river, two houses that want it. Every week a few more men drown in it.

choices.label: Give the ford to the crown
text: The King's men hold the ford; both houses pay to cross.
The crown holds the ford, and both houses pay to cross it.
Royal men keep the ford; each house pays its crossing.
The ford's tolls come to Kingsmere every season.
Every season, the ford's tolls arrive at Kingsmere.
Kingsmere collects the ford tolls season by season.

choices.label: Give it to {house}
text: {house} holds the ford by the King's grant.
The ford belongs to {house} by royal grant.
By the King's grant, {house} keeps the ford.

choices.label: Build a second bridge
text: Masons build a bridge upriver; neither house need fight.
Upriver, masons raise a bridge, and neither house need fight.
A second bridge goes up, leaving nothing to fight over.
The ford runs red every spring.
Each spring the ford runs red.
The ford is bloodied every spring.

cards.subject: war_pair
cards.title: A peace feast for {house} and {rival}
cards.text: A herald says both houses are tired. A feast at the King's table might end it, or start it again over the wine.

choices.label: Host the feast
text: {house} and {rival} drink at Kingsmere, swords at the door.
{house} and {rival} share wine at Kingsmere, their swords left at the door.
Swords at the door, {house} and {rival} drink together at Kingsmere.
The peace made at the King's table holds through the season.
The peace sworn at the King's table lasts the season.
What was agreed over the King's wine holds for the season.

choices.label: Make them swear on the relics
text: Both lords swear peace before the gods.
Before the gods, both lords swear to keep the peace.
The two lords take oath on the relics.

choices.label: Let them bleed
text: The King has better uses for wine.
The King finds better things to do with his wine.
No feast; the King's wine is kept for better use.
The war goes on; the herald goes home.
The herald returns home, and the war continues.
The war rolls on, and the herald goes back.

cards.subject: war_pair
cards.title: {house} sends the King a share of plunder
cards.text: {lord} has sacked one of {rival}'s villages and sends the crown a cart of silver plate.

choices.label: Take it
text: The plate goes to the treasury; {rival} hears of it.
The treasury takes the plate, and {rival} hears about it.
{rival} learns its plate now sits in the King's treasury.

choices.label: Send it back to {rival}
text: The plate goes home to {rival} with the King's regrets.
The plate returns to {rival} along with the King's apologies.
With the King's regrets, {rival} gets its plate back.

choices.label: Give it to the burned village
text: The village gets its plate back, and a new roof.
The village has its plate again, and a new roof as well.
The burned village gets back its plate, and a roof besides.
The village tells everyone the King is just.
The village tells all comers that the King is just.
The King's justice is the village's favourite tale.
The plate sits in the courtyard; everyone knows whose it was.
The plate lies in the courtyard, and all know its owner.
Nobody touches the plate in the courtyard; everyone knows whose it is.

cards.subject: house_warm
cards.title: {lord} asks leave to go to war
cards.text: {house} has an old grudge against a neighbour, and {lord} wants the King's blessing to settle it.

choices.label: Give your blessing
text: {lord} rides out with the King's leave.
With the King's leave, {lord} rides to war.
{lord} rides out, blessed by the crown.
{house} comes home with new fields, and new enemies.
{house} returns with new fields and new foes.
New lands for {house}, and new enemies with them.

choices.label: Forbid it
text: {lord} sheathes the sword, for now.
{lord} puts away the sword, for the present.
The sword goes back in its scabbard; {lord} waits.

choices.label: Settle the grudge at court
text: The King hears both houses and splits the difference.
The King hears both houses and divides the difference.
At court, the grudge is heard and split down the middle.
{lord} goes to war without asking.
{lord} marches to war unasked.
Without the King's leave, {lord} goes to war.

cards.subject: hungry_town
cards.title: Bread riot in {town}
cards.text: The bakers of {town} have no flour and the crowd thinks they are lying. Ovens are being smashed.

choices.label: Send grain and soldiers
text: Carts and spears roll into {town} together.
Grain carts and spearmen enter {town} side by side.
{town} receives grain and soldiers at once.

choices.label: Soldiers only
text: The King's men clear {town}'s streets with staves.
With staves, the King's men clear the streets of {town}.
Soldiers beat {town}'s streets clear.
{town} remembers the staves at harvest.
At harvest, {town} remembers the staves.
{town} has not forgotten the staves when harvest comes.

choices.label: Throw open the lord's barns
text: {house}'s own barns are opened to {town} by the King's word.
By the King's word, {house}'s barns are opened to {town}.
{town} eats from the barns of {house}, at the King's order.
{town} burns its bakeries and goes hungrier.
{town} burns its bakeries, and goes hungrier for it.
The bakeries of {town} are burned, and there is less bread than before.

cards.subject: hungry_town
cards.title: {town} sends its children away
cards.text: Mothers in {town} put their children on carts to anywhere with bread. The roads fill with them.

choices.label: Take them in at Kingsmere
text: The King's halls fill with {town}'s children.
{town}'s children fill the halls of Kingsmere.
The King takes {town}'s children into his halls.
{town}'s children grow up the King's own people.
{town}'s children grow up as the King's own.
Raised at Kingsmere, the children of {town} belong to the King.

choices.label: Send bread to {town} so they can stay
text: Bread carts meet the children on the road.
The bread carts meet the children along the road.
On the road, the children find bread coming to them.

choices.label: Close the roads
text: The children turn back to {town}.
The children turn around and go back to {town}.
With the roads closed, the children return to {town}.
The children of {town} go where they can.
{town}'s children scatter wherever they can.
The children of {town} go wherever will have them.

cards.subject: hungry_town
cards.title: {town} eats its horses
cards.text: The last horses in {town} are going into the pot. Without them there will be no ploughing.

choices.label: Send plough oxen for spring
text: Oxen are driven to {town} under the crown's brand.
Oxen with the crown's brand are driven to {town}.
{town} receives plough oxen bearing the royal brand.
{town}'s fields are ploughed in time; the harvest comes.
{town} ploughs in time, and the harvest follows.
The fields of {town} are ploughed, and a harvest comes.

choices.label: Send grain so the horses live
text: Grain reaches {town}; the horses are spared.
The grain arrives in {town}, and the horses live.
{town} spares its horses, fed on the crown's grain.

choices.label: Let them eat
text: {town} eats tonight, and starves next year.
{town} eats tonight, and will starve next year.
Tonight {town} has meat; next year it has nothing.
{town}'s fields lie fallow without horses.
With no horses, {town}'s fields go unploughed.
{town}'s fields lie idle, the horses eaten.
{town} eats its horses and its seed corn.
{town} eats its horses, and its seed corn after them.
The horses go into {town}'s pots, and the seed corn too.

cards.subject: hungry_town
cards.title: Terrible rumours from {town}
cards.text: Travellers whisper about what the starving of {town} eat now. Nobody wants to say it at court.

choices.label: Send the royal granary's last
text: The last of the crown's grain goes to {town}.
The crown sends {town} the last of its grain.
{town} gets the final sacks from the royal granary.

choices.label: Send priests and a physician
text: The priests go to {town} and pray over what they find.
The priests reach {town} and pray over what they see.
In {town}, the priests pray over what they find.

choices.label: Close {town} to travellers
text: {town} is sealed until the hunger passes.
{town} is shut until the hunger is over.
No one enters or leaves {town} till the hunger passes.
The tales from sealed {town} grow worse in every telling.
Tales from shut-up {town} grow darker each time they are told.
Every retelling of what happened in {town} is worse than the last.
The whispers about {town} reach every hall.
Every hall hears the whispers about {town}.
The talk of {town} reaches all the great halls.

cards.subject: realm
cards.title: A grain ship offers its cargo
cards.text: A southern captain has a hold full of wheat, and he knows what it is worth in a hungry realm.

choices.label: Pay his price
text: The wheat comes ashore and goes inland.
The wheat is landed and carried inland.
Ashore comes the wheat, and off it goes inland.

choices.label: Seize the ship
text: The captain is put ashore; the wheat is the crown's.
The captain is set ashore, and the crown takes the wheat.
The wheat belongs to the crown now; the captain stands on the dock.
No southern ship will dock in the King's harbours.
No ship from the south will put in at the King's harbours.
The southern ships shun the King's ports.

choices.label: Haggle him down
text: The captain sells for less, and sails off muttering.
The captain sells cheaper, and leaves grumbling.
Beaten down on price, the captain sails away muttering.
The captain sold half his grain to a great house instead.
The captain sold half his cargo to a great house instead.
Half the grain went to a great house, not the crown.
The ship sails on to a richer harbour.
The ship goes on to a wealthier port.
A richer harbour gets the grain ship.

cards.subject: realm
cards.title: Deserters on the roads
cards.text: Men are slipping away from the levies with their spears. Some go home; some go into the woods.

choices.label: Hang the deserters you catch
text: Gibbets go up at the crossroads.
Gibbets rise at the crossroads.
The crossroads get their gibbets.

choices.label: Pay the levy on time
text: The crown's pay chests ride out to every camp.
Pay chests from the crown reach every camp.
Every camp is paid on time from the crown's chests.

choices.label: Let the farmers go home
text: The levy thins; the fields fill.
The levy shrinks, and the fields are full of hands.
Farmers go home; fewer spears, more ploughs.
A thin levy meets the trouble.
The trouble is met by a thin levy.
Only a thin levy stands against the trouble.
The deserters become bandits.
The deserters turn to banditry.
Bandits are what the deserters become.

cards.subject: realm
cards.title: A spy from the enemy camp
cards.text: A man was taken near the walls with a map of Kingsmere's gates sewn into his coat.

choices.label: Make him talk
text: The spy talks; the King learns the enemy's numbers.
The spy speaks, and the King learns how many the enemy are.
Under questioning, the spy gives up the enemy's numbers.

choices.label: Send him back with a false map
text: The spy goes home with the wrong gates.
The spy returns home with the gates all wrong.
A false map rides home with the spy.
The enemy's men come to the wrong gate.
The enemy arrives at the wrong gate.
The wrong gate is where the enemy comes.

choices.label: Hang him from the gate
text: The spy hangs where his friends can see him.
The spy hangs in sight of his friends.
From the gate the spy hangs, for his friends to see.
The spy slips his ropes in the night.
In the night, the spy gets out of his ropes.
The spy is gone by morning, his ropes empty.

cards.subject: seat
cards.title: Kingsmere's walls are old
cards.text: The master mason says the north wall is more ivy than stone. With trouble coming, someone should mend it.

choices.label: Mend it now, whatever the cost
text: Masons swarm the north wall.
The north wall crawls with masons.
Masons descend on the north wall in numbers.

choices.label: Patch the worst of it
text: Timber and earth fill the cracks.
The cracks are stuffed with timber and earth.
Earth and timber plug the worst of the gaps.

choices.label: The walls have stood a hundred years
text: The ivy stays.
The ivy is left alone.
Nobody touches the ivy.
The north wall slumps in the rain.
In the rain, the north wall sags.
Rain brings the north wall slumping down.
The north wall crumbles a little more.
A little more of the north wall falls away.
The north wall crumbles on, a stone at a time.

cards.subject: realm
cards.title: The lords sit on their hands
cards.text: With trouble on the march, the great houses send letters full of excuses and no spears.

choices.label: Shame them in open court
text: The King reads their letters aloud at Kingsmere.
At Kingsmere, the King reads their letters out loud.
Their letters are read before the whole court by the King.

choices.label: Buy their spears
text: Silver goes out; spears come in.
Silver leaves the treasury, and spears arrive.
The crown pays, and the lords' spears come.

choices.label: Fight without them
text: The crown stands alone.
The crown faces it by itself.
Alone, the crown takes the field.
The lords who held back now say the King needed no help.
The lords who hung back now claim the King never needed them.
Having stayed home, the lords now say the King managed fine without them.
The lords wait to see who wins.
The lords bide their time to see who prevails.
The lords hold back and watch for the winner.

cards.subject: realm
cards.title: The old lords call the King a boy
cards.text: In the first seasons of a reign the grey lords test the crown. One of them yawned through the King's speech.

choices.label: Make an example of him
text: The yawning lord loses his seat at court.
The lord who yawned no longer has a seat at court.
His seat at court is taken from the yawning lord.
No lord yawns at court now.
Nobody yawns at court anymore.
The court has stopped yawning.

choices.label: Win them over at table
text: A season of feasts for the grey lords.
The grey lords are feasted for a season.
A whole season of suppers for the old lords.

choices.label: Let deeds answer
text: The King says nothing and gets to work.
Without a word, the King sets to work.
The King answers nothing, and works.
The grey lords keep yawning.
The grey lords go on yawning.
The yawning among the old lords continues.

cards.subject: realm
cards.title: The coronation is still unpaid
cards.text: The goldsmiths who made the crown want paying. So do the cooks, the heralds and the man who hired out the tents.

choices.label: Pay them all
text: The crown's first debts are settled.
The crown settles its first debts.
All the coronation debts are paid.

choices.label: Pay the goldsmiths only
text: The cooks and heralds wait, and talk.
Cooks and heralds go unpaid, and gossip.
The goldsmiths are paid; the cooks and heralds wait and talk.
The unpaid heralds sing rude verses in the taverns.
The heralds, still unpaid, sing coarse verses in the taverns.
In the taverns, the unpaid heralds sing rude songs of the crown.

choices.label: Tell them it was an honour to serve
text: The tradesmen of Kingsmere remember it.
Kingsmere's tradesmen do not forget it.
The honour is remembered by the tradesmen of Kingsmere.
The goldsmiths' guild sues the crown before the temple.
Before the temple, the goldsmiths' guild brings suit against the crown.
The crown is taken to law by the goldsmiths' guild.

cards.subject: seat
cards.title: The King's first hanging
cards.text: A horse thief waits on the scaffold at {town}. The crowd wants to see what kind of king they have.

choices.label: Pardon him
text: The thief walks free; the crowd cheers a merciful king.
The thief goes free, and the crowd cheers its merciful King.
Pardoned, the thief walks away to the crowd's applause.
Every thief in {town} expects a pardon now.
Every thief in {town} now counts on a pardon.
{town}'s thieves all expect mercy now.

choices.label: Let it be done
text: The rope is used; the crowd goes home thinking.
The rope does its work, and the crowd goes home thoughtful.
The thief hangs; the crowd leaves quieter than it came.

choices.label: Send him to the levy instead
text: The thief marches with the King's spears.
The thief now marches among the King's spears.
Into the levy goes the thief.
The thief is hanged without the King, and the crowd notes it.
The thief is hanged without the King's word, and the crowd marks it.
The crowd sees a hanging the King had no part in.

cards.subject: realm
cards.title: The treasury is nearly bare
cards.text: The steward turns the last chest on its side. The guards' pay is due next season.

choices.label: Melt the royal plate
text: The King eats off pewter; the guards are paid.
The guards are paid, and the King dines off pewter.
The royal plate is melted down; the guards get their wages.

choices.label: Borrow from the moneylenders
text: The moneylenders open their chests, and their ledgers.
The moneylenders open their chests and their ledgers both.
Silver comes from the moneylenders, with ink attached.
The moneylenders come for their silver, and more.
The moneylenders come to collect their silver, and then some.
The loan comes due, and the moneylenders want more than they gave.

choices.label: A special levy on every house
text: Every great house pays toward the crown.
All the great houses pay toward the crown.
The special levy is paid by every great house.
The guards go unpaid, and grumble at the gates.
The guards go without pay, and mutter at the gates.
At the gates, unpaid guards grumble.

cards.subject: realm
cards.title: The steward has never seen so much silver
cards.text: The treasury's chests are full. The lords notice, and so do the beggars.

choices.label: Build something to be remembered by
text: A royal work is begun at Kingsmere.
At Kingsmere, a royal work is started.
The King begins a great work at Kingsmere.
The King's great work stands; travellers come to see it.
The King's great work stands, and travellers come to look.
Travellers journey to see what the King built.

choices.label: Give a gift to every house
text: Every great house gets a chest from the King.
Each great house receives a chest from the King.
The King sends a chest to every great house.

choices.label: Keep it; lean years come
text: The chests stay full, and closely watched.
The chests stay full, and well guarded.
The treasury is kept full, and closely watched.
The lords whisper that the King is a miser.
The lords murmur that the King is a miser.
Whispers go round that the King hoards his silver.

cards.subject: seat
cards.title: The steward's new house
cards.text: The steward has built a fine house in {town}. The steward's pay would not build a henhouse.

choices.label: Audit the books
text: The King's clerks open the steward's ledgers.
The steward's ledgers are opened by the King's clerks.
Royal clerks go through the steward's books.
The steward's thefts are found and repaid.
The steward's thefts are uncovered, and paid back.
What the steward took is found and returned.

choices.label: Dismiss him quietly
text: A new steward takes the keys.
The keys pass to a new steward.
Quietly, a new steward is installed.

choices.label: A good steward deserves a good house
text: The steward keeps the house, and the habit.
The steward keeps the house, and keeps his habits.
His house stays, and so does his thieving.
The steward's thefts grow bolder.
The steward steals more boldly.
Bolder thefts follow from the steward.
The steward builds a stable next.
Next, the steward builds himself a stable.
A stable is the steward's next building.

cards.subject: realm
cards.title: The Hand and the Marshal at each other's throats
cards.text: Every council the Hand and the Marshal shout over each other. The clerks have stopped writing it down.

choices.label: Side with the Hand
text: The Marshal sulks among his soldiers.
The Marshal broods among his soldiers.
Among his men, the Marshal sulks.
The Marshal's men are slow to answer the Hand's orders.
The Marshal's men take their time with the Hand's orders.
The Hand's orders reach the Marshal's men and move slowly.

choices.label: Side with the Marshal
text: The Hand counts coins louder than before.
The Hand counts coins more loudly than ever.
Coins clink louder in the Hand's counting room.
The Hand's purse is slow to pay the Marshal's men.
The Hand pays the Marshal's men slowly.
The Marshal's men wait long on the Hand's purse.

choices.label: Make them dine together
text: A long, silent supper. Then a slightly less silent one.
A long, quiet supper, then one a little less quiet.
The first supper is silent; the second, slightly less so.
The council stops deciding anything.
The council decides nothing at all.
Nothing is decided at council anymore.

cards.subject: seat
cards.title: A painter wants to paint the King
cards.text: A famous painter from abroad offers a portrait of the King, for a price, and a season of sittings.

choices.label: Sit for the portrait
text: The portrait hangs in {town}'s great hall.
{town}'s great hall gets the portrait.
In the great hall of {town}, the portrait is hung.
The King's portrait is copied for every great house.
Every great house gets a copy of the King's portrait.
Copies of the portrait go to all the great houses.

choices.label: Have him paint the court instead
text: The painter sketches the lords; the lords love it.
The painter draws the lords, and the lords are delighted.
The lords adore the painter's sketches of themselves.

choices.label: The King has no time for sittings
text: The painter goes to a rival court.
The painter leaves for a rival court.
A rival court gains the painter.
The painter paints a great lord instead, in the King's pose.
The painter paints a great lord instead, posed as the King.
A great lord sits for the painter, in the King's own pose.

cards.subject: seat
cards.title: The astrologer's warning
cards.text: The court astrologer says the stars warn against travel this year. The King has three journeys planned.

choices.label: Stay home
text: The journeys are cancelled; the lords who expected the King wait.
The journeys are called off, and the lords who expected the King wait.
The King stays home; the lords who looked for him wait on.

choices.label: Travel anyway
text: The King rides out; the astrologer wrings his hands.
The King rides out while the astrologer wrings his hands.
The astrologer frets as the King takes to the road.
The King returned safe; the astrologer looks for a new post.
The King came back safe; the astrologer seeks other work.
Home unharmed, the King leaves the astrologer looking for a new post.

choices.label: Find a better astrologer
text: A new astrologer reads kinder stars.
The new astrologer finds kinder stars.
A different astrologer reads the heavens more gently.
The astrologer tells everyone what the stars said.
The astrologer tells all and sundry what the stars said.
Everyone hears the stars' verdict from the astrologer.

cards.subject: realm
cards.title: A foreign envoy will not kneel
cards.text: An envoy from over the sea stands upright before the throne. The court holds its breath.

choices.label: Make him kneel
text: The guards bend his knee for him.
The guards bend the envoy's knee for him.
His knee is bent by the guards.
Over the sea they call the King a tyrant, and tax his ships.
Across the sea, they call the King a tyrant and tax his ships.
The King is named tyrant overseas, and his ships pay for it.

choices.label: Laugh and wave him on
text: The envoy speaks standing; some lords think the King weak.
The envoy speaks on his feet, and some lords call the King weak.
Standing, the envoy has his say; a few lords think the King soft.

choices.label: Rise and greet him as an equal
text: The King steps down to the envoy; the court gasps.
The court gasps as the King steps down to meet the envoy.
The King comes down to the envoy, and the court draws breath.
The envoy's country sends ships of trade.
Trade ships arrive from the envoy's country.
The envoy's land sends merchant ships.
The envoy leaves, unseen and unpleased.
The envoy departs unseen and displeased.
Unreceived, the envoy goes, and not happily.

cards.subject: realm
cards.title: The King's cousin marries
cards.text: The King's cousin weds a minor lady. A royal wedding means a royal feast, or a royal slight.

choices.label: A feast fit for a prince
text: Every house sends someone; everyone eats.
Every house sends someone, and all of them eat.
All the houses come, and the tables are cleared.

choices.label: A family supper
text: The cousin is wed quietly, and resents it.
The cousin weds quietly, and holds it against the King.
A small supper for the cousin's wedding, and a lasting resentment.
The cousin leaves court for the cold houses' company.
The cousin quits court for the company of the cold houses.
The cold houses gain the cousin's company.

choices.label: Let the bride's family pay
text: The bride's family feast the realm, and own the day.
The bride's family feasts the realm, and the day is theirs.
The day belongs to the bride's family, who pay for it.
The cousin weds without the King's blessing.
The cousin marries without the King's blessing.
Unblessed by the King, the cousin weds.

cards.subject: realm
cards.title: Knights errant at court
cards.text: A band of landless knights asks to serve the King. They have more swords than manners.

choices.label: Take them into the guard
text: The knights eat the King's bread and wear his colours.
The knights wear the King's colours and eat his bread.
The guard gains knights, fed and dressed by the crown.

choices.label: Send them against the outlaws
text: The knights ride off to hunt for glory and bandits.
Off go the knights, hunting bandits and glory.
The knights ride out after outlaws and renown.
The knights errant clear the King's roads of thieves.
The knights errant rid the King's roads of thieves.
Thieves are cleared from the roads by the wandering knights.

choices.label: No more mouths at court
text: The knights ride on to a lord who will feed them.
The knights move on to a lord who will feed them.
A lord with a fuller table gets the knights.
The knights errant fight for a great house now.
The knights errant now fight for a great house.
A great house has the knights errant in its pay.
The knights brawl in Kingsmere's taverns.
The knights brawl through Kingsmere's taverns.
Kingsmere's taverns suffer the knights' brawling.

cards.subject: realm
cards.title: The lords grow fat in peace
cards.text: Years without war, and the lords are bored. Boredom makes plotters.

choices.label: Hold a great tourney
text: The lords break lances instead of oaths.
Lances are broken instead of oaths.
The lords shatter lances rather than their vows.

choices.label: Send them on a crusade abroad
text: The restless young lords sail away to a far war.
The restless young lords sail off to a distant war.
A far war takes the restless young lords.
The young lords come home scarred, and humbler.
The young lords return scarred and humbled.
Home come the young lords, marked and meeker.

choices.label: Let them plot; it keeps them busy
text: The plotting starts.
The plotting begins.
Plots begin to form.
A plot against the crown is whispered of.
There is whispering of a plot against the crown.
A plot against the King is spoken of in corners.
Boredom finds its own amusement.
Boredom makes its own fun.
Idle lords find their own amusements.

cards.subject: realm
cards.title: Who comes after the King?
cards.text: The King's hair is greying. The lords ask, less quietly each year, who will wear the crown next.

choices.label: Name an heir before the court
text: The heir is proclaimed at Kingsmere.
At Kingsmere, the heir is proclaimed.
The court hears the heir named.
The lords court the heir now, as much as the King.
The lords now court the heir as much as the King.
The heir draws as many lords as the King does.

choices.label: Say the gods will choose
text: The question hangs over every feast.
Every feast has the question hanging over it.
The succession sits unspoken at every table.

choices.label: Make the lords swear to whoever you name later
text: The lords swear to a name not yet spoken.
The lords swear loyalty to a name yet unspoken.
An oath is sworn to an heir not yet named.
Each great house backs its own heir in whispers.
In whispers, each great house backs an heir of its own.
Every great house quietly favours its own claimant.

cards.subject: seat
cards.title: The chronicler wants the King's own words
cards.text: The court chronicler is writing the history of the reign and wants to hear it from the King's mouth.

choices.label: Tell it all, the bad with the good
text: The chronicle is honest; the lords read it with surprise.
The chronicle tells the truth, and the lords are surprised by it.
The lords read an honest chronicle, and wonder at it.

choices.label: Tell only the triumphs
text: The chronicle shines; nobody believes all of it.
The chronicle gleams, and no one believes every word.
A shining chronicle, which nobody quite trusts.
Later readers call the chronicle flattery.
Later readers say the chronicle flatters.
Those who come after call it flattery.

choices.label: Pay him to write it himself
text: The chronicler writes what he thinks the King wants.
The chronicler writes what he supposes the King would like.
Paid, the chronicler guesses at the King's wishes and writes those.
The chronicler writes it from tavern talk.
The chronicler builds it from tavern gossip.
Tavern talk is the chronicler's source.

cards.subject: realm
cards.title: An old enemy's son comes to court
cards.text: The son of a lord the King once broke asks to serve. He smiles a great deal.

choices.label: Take him into service
text: He serves, and smiles.
He serves, smiling.
The son takes service, still smiling.
The son serves faithfully; the old feud is buried.
The son serves loyally, and the old feud is laid to rest.
The feud is buried; the son proves faithful.

choices.label: Watch him closely
text: A spy sleeps outside the son's door.
A spy beds down outside the son's door.
The son sleeps with a spy at his door.

choices.label: Send him away
text: The son leaves, still smiling.
The son goes, smiling still.
Sent away, the son leaves with his smile intact.
The son is seen at a cold house's table.
The son is seen dining with a cold house.
A cold house has the son at its table.
The son finds another lord to serve.
The son takes service with another lord.
Another lord gains the son's service.

cards.subject: realm
cards.title: A southern prince offers an alliance
cards.text: A prince from beyond the hills sends an envoy: spears for the King's wars, ports for his ships.

choices.label: Sign the alliance
text: The King's seal goes on the treaty.
The treaty bears the King's seal.
The King seals the alliance.
The southern prince calls on the alliance; the crown must send men.
The southern prince invokes the alliance, and the crown must send men.
Men must march south; the prince has called on the treaty.

choices.label: Trade only, no spears
text: A trading treaty is signed.
A treaty of trade is signed.
The crown signs for trade alone.
Southern ships fill the King's ports with goods.
The King's ports fill with goods from southern ships.
Southern ships crowd the harbours with cargo.

choices.label: No foreign ties
text: The envoy goes home.
The envoy returns home.
Home goes the envoy.
The southern prince signs with a great house instead.
The southern prince makes his treaty with a great house.
A great house signs with the southern prince in the King's place.

cards.subject: seat
cards.title: The King's physician quarrels with the priests
cards.text: The physician wants to cut and study the dead; the priests say it is a sin.

choices.label: Side with the physician
text: The physician studies; the priests preach against it.
The physician studies, and the priests preach against him.
The priests rail from the pulpit while the physician works.
The physician's learning saves a lord's heir at {town}.
At {town}, a lord's heir lives by the physician's learning.
The physician's study saves a lord's heir in {town}.

choices.label: Side with the priests
text: The physician burns his notes.
The physician's notes go into the fire.
The physician burns his work.

choices.label: Let him study in secret
text: The physician works by night, behind locked doors.
The physician works at night behind locked doors.
Behind bolted doors, the physician studies by candle.
The priests drive the physician out of {town}.
The priests hound the physician from {town}.
{town} sees its physician driven out by the priests.

cards.subject: seat
cards.title: A song about the King in {town}'s taverns
cards.text: Every tavern in {town} is singing a new song about the King. It is not kind.
