choices.label: Find the singer and reward a better song
text: The singer writes a kinder verse, for a purse.
For a purse, the singer writes a gentler verse.
Paid, the singer finds kinder words.

choices.label: Ban the song
text: The song is banned, so everyone sings it louder.
Banned, the song is sung all the louder.
The ban only makes the song louder.
The banned song is sung in every town now.
Every town now sings the banned song.
The forbidden song is heard in every town.

choices.label: Sing it yourself at supper
text: The King sings the song at his own table; the court roars.
The court roars as the King sings it at his own table.
At supper the King sings the song himself, and the hall howls.
The taverns of {town} sing the King's own verse now, and laugh with him.
{town}'s taverns now sing the King's own verse, laughing along with him.
In {town}, the taverns sing the King's version, and laugh with the King.
The song spreads to the next town.
The song travels on to the next town.
The next town takes up the song.

cards.subject: seat
cards.title: A stone is missing from the crown
cards.text: The great red stone in the crown has been prised out and replaced with glass. Nobody knows when.

choices.label: Turn the castle upside down
text: Every room at {town} is searched.
Each room at {town} is searched.
{town} is searched from cellar to tower.
The stone is found sewn into a page's jacket.
The stone turns up sewn into a page's jacket.
A page's jacket is found to hold the stone.

choices.label: Wear the glass and say nothing
text: The King wears glass; nobody notices.
The King wears glass, and no one is the wiser.
Nobody notices the glass in the King's crown.
A jeweller in a great house sells a famous red stone.
A jeweller of a great house sells a famous red stone.
A famous red stone is sold by a great house's jeweller.

choices.label: Offer a reward for its return
text: A reward is cried in every market.
Every market hears the reward cried.
Criers call the reward in all the markets.
The stone comes back, wrapped in a beggar's rag.
Wrapped in a beggar's rag, the stone returns.
A beggar's rag brings the stone back.
The theft becomes a joke at court.
The court makes a joke of the theft.
The theft is laughed about at court.

cards.subject: realm
cards.title: The old chancellor wants to retire
cards.text: The chancellor who served three kings asks leave to go home. Nobody else knows where the papers are.

choices.label: Give him a pension and a manor
text: The old chancellor retires in honour.
The old chancellor is retired with honour.
A pension and a manor see the chancellor off in honour.

choices.label: Ask him to stay one more year
text: The chancellor sighs, and stays.
The chancellor sighs and stays on.
With a sigh, the chancellor agrees to another year.
The old chancellor dies at his desk, papers in order.
The old chancellor dies at his desk, his papers in order.
At his desk, papers tidy, the old chancellor dies.

choices.label: Let him go
text: The chancellor goes; the papers are a mess for a season.
The chancellor leaves, and the papers are in disorder for a season.
A season of muddled papers follows the chancellor's going.
The chancellor leaves without a farewell.
The chancellor departs with no farewell.
No farewell is said; the chancellor is gone.

cards.subject: realm
cards.title: The lords say the crown hoards grain
cards.text: Word is going round that Kingsmere's granaries are full while the realm goes hungry.

choices.label: Open the granaries to the lords
text: The lords' carts fill at Kingsmere.
At Kingsmere, the lords' carts are filled.
The lords load their carts at the royal granaries.

choices.label: Show the empty granaries
text: The lords are walked through bare barns.
The lords are led through empty barns.
Bare barns are shown to the lords.

choices.label: Let them talk
text: The rumour grows with the hunger.
As hunger grows, so does the rumour.
The rumour feeds on the hunger.
The lords repeat the rumour as fact.
The lords repeat the rumour as though it were true.
What was rumour, the lords now tell as fact.
The rumour becomes the truth people tell.
The rumour turns into the story everyone believes.
What people tell now is the rumour, called truth.

cards.subject: realm
cards.title: Wolves on the winter roads
cards.text: Couriers come in with torn cloaks. The packs are bold this year.

choices.label: Escort every courier
text: Couriers ride with spears this winter.
This winter, couriers ride with spearmen.
Every courier has spears beside him this winter.

choices.label: Pay a bounty on wolves
text: Wolf pelts pile up at every town gate.
Every town gate has its pile of wolf pelts.
Wolf skins heap up at the gates.
The roads are quieter; the bounty did it.
The bounty did its work; the roads are quieter.
With the bounty paid, the roads grow calmer.

choices.label: The couriers ride fast enough
text: A courier goes missing.
One courier does not arrive.
A courier vanishes on the road.
A courier's horse comes back without him.
A courier's horse returns riderless.
The horse comes home; the courier does not.
The King's letters arrive late, if at all.
The King's letters come late, or not at all.
Royal letters arrive late, when they arrive.

cards.subject: crown_town
cards.title: Spring floods at {town}
cards.text: The meltwater burst the dykes at {town}. Fields are lakes; cottages are islands.

choices.label: Rebuild the dykes in stone
text: Stone dykes rise around {town}'s fields.
Around {town}'s fields, dykes of stone are raised.
{town}'s fields are ringed with stone dykes.
The next flood breaks on {town}'s new dykes and goes no further.
The next flood breaks against {town}'s new dykes and stops.
{town}'s stone dykes hold back the next flood.

choices.label: Send boats and bread
text: Boats ferry {town}'s folk to dry ground.
Boats carry the people of {town} to dry land.
{town}'s folk are ferried to high ground.

choices.label: The water will go down
text: The water goes down, slowly.
Slowly, the water falls.
The flood recedes, in its own time.
{town}'s spring sowing is lost.
{town} loses its spring sowing.
The spring sowing at {town} is washed away.

cards.subject: house_any
cards.title: {house} disputes the harvest tithe
cards.text: {lord} says the crown's reeves counted the sheaves twice. {house}'s barns at {town} say otherwise.

choices.label: Recount the sheaves
text: The reeves count again at {town}.
The reeves recount at {town}.
At {town}, the sheaves are counted again.
The recount finds {house} was right.
The recount shows {house} had it right.
{house} was right, the recount finds.

choices.label: The tithe stands
text: {house} pays, and protests.
{house} pays under protest.
The tithe is paid by {house}, with complaint.

choices.label: Halve it for {house}
text: {house} pays half; other houses ask why.
{house} pays half, and the other houses want to know why.
Half from {house}; the other houses ask about their own.
{house} pays nothing this autumn.
This autumn, {house} pays nothing.
No tithe comes from {house} this autumn.

cards.subject: house_any
cards.title: A wedding ends in blood at {town}
cards.text: At a wedding in {house}'s hall, an old feud came out with the wine. Two guests are dead.

choices.label: Send the King's justice
text: A royal judge rides to {town}.
A judge of the King's rides to {town}.
{town} receives a royal judge.
The killers hang; {house} says the King's justice is fair.
The killers hang, and {house} calls the King's justice fair.
{house} watches the killers hang, and says the crown judged fairly.

choices.label: Leave it to {lord}
text: {lord} judges in their own hall.
{lord} sits in judgement in their own hall.
In their own hall, {lord} gives judgement.

choices.label: Fine every family there
text: Every family at the wedding pays the crown.
Each family at the wedding pays the crown.
The crown fines every family that attended.
The feud spreads through {house}'s lands.
The feud spreads across the lands of {house}.
{house}'s lands are caught up in the feud.

cards.subject: house_warm
cards.title: {house} founds a monastery
cards.text: {lord} would found a monastery near {town} and name the King its patron.

choices.label: Be its patron
text: The King's name is carved over the gate at {town}.
Over the gate at {town}, the King's name is carved.
{town}'s monastery bears the King's name above its gate.

choices.label: Let {house} have the honour
text: {house}'s name alone goes over the gate.
Only {house}'s name is carved over the gate.
The gate carries the name of {house} and no other.

choices.label: Land for monks is land lost to tithe
text: {lord} builds it smaller.
{lord} builds on a smaller scale.
{lord} builds a modest one.
{house} builds it, and names a saint instead of the King.
{house} builds it, naming a saint rather than the King.
A saint's name, not the King's, goes on {house}'s monastery.

cards.subject: house_cold
cards.title: {house} shelters a heretic preacher
cards.text: A preacher who calls the King's priests liars is living at {town} as {lord}'s guest.

choices.label: Demand they hand him over
text: {lord} is ordered to hand the preacher to the King's priests.
{lord} is told to give the preacher up to the King's priests.
The order goes to {lord}: surrender the preacher to the crown's priests.

choices.label: Let him preach
text: The preacher preaches; the priests are furious.
The preacher preaches, and the priests rage.
The priests fume while the preacher speaks.
The preacher's followers grow in {town}.
In {town}, the preacher's following grows.
More of {town} follows the preacher.

choices.label: Invite him to debate at court
text: The preacher comes to Kingsmere to argue with the high priest.
The preacher comes to Kingsmere to dispute with the high priest.
At Kingsmere, the preacher and the high priest argue it out.
The debate is the talk of the realm; both sides claim victory.
All the realm talks of the debate, and each side says it won.
The debate is on every tongue; both sides call it a victory.
The preacher's words spread from {town}.
From {town}, the preacher's words spread.
The preacher's teaching travels out of {town}.

cards.subject: house_warm
cards.title: {lord} offers a champion
cards.text: {house} has a giant of a knight, and {lord} would see him fight under the King's banner.

choices.label: Make him the King's champion
text: The giant stands at the King's right hand.
The giant takes his place at the King's right hand.
At the King's right hand stands the giant.

choices.label: Let him fight in the lists
text: The giant unhorses every knight in the realm.
Every knight in the realm is unhorsed by the giant.
The giant knocks each knight of the realm from his saddle.

choices.label: The King has knights enough
text: The giant goes home to {town}.
The giant returns home to {town}.
Back to {town} goes the giant.
The giant fights for a rival court.
A rival court gets the giant's sword.
The giant takes service at a rival court.

cards.subject: realm
cards.title: Foreign merchants want a fair
cards.text: Merchants from over the sea would hold a great fair in the realm, if the King guarantees their safety.

choices.label: Guarantee it with the King's guard
text: The fair is held under the crown's banner.
The fair is held beneath the crown's banner.
Under royal colours, the fair goes ahead.
The foreign fair comes every year now, and pays well.
The foreign fair now returns each year, and pays handsomely.
Every year the foreign merchants come back, and pay well.

choices.label: Guarantee it with words
text: The fair comes; a merchant is robbed.
The fair arrives, and a merchant is robbed.
A merchant is robbed at the fair.
The robbed merchant tells every port of it.
The robbed merchant tells the tale in every port.
Every port hears of the merchant who was robbed.

choices.label: Our own merchants come first
text: The guilds cheer; the foreigners stay home.
The guilds cheer, and the foreigners stay away.
No foreigners come; the guilds are delighted.
The fair goes to a great house's town instead.
A great house's town gets the fair instead.
The fair goes to a town of a great house.

cards.subject: crown_town
cards.title: {town}'s weavers want a monopoly
cards.text: The weavers of {town} want no cloth sold there but theirs. They offer the crown a fee for it.

choices.label: Sell them the monopoly
text: {town}'s weavers pay, and raise their prices.
{town}'s weavers pay for it, then put up their prices.
The weavers of {town} buy the monopoly and charge more.

choices.label: Refuse; trade stays free
text: The weavers sulk at their looms.
The weavers sulk over their looms.
At their looms, the weavers mope.
Cheap cloth floods {town}; the weavers grumble, the people don't.
{town} fills with cheap cloth; the weavers grumble, but the people do not.
Cheap cloth pours into {town}, pleasing all but the weavers.

choices.label: Grant it for ten years only
text: The weavers pay a little, and plan to ask again.
The weavers pay a little, and mean to ask again.
A small fee from the weavers, and a plan to return.
The weavers break the looms of anyone who competes.
The weavers smash the looms of any rival.
Any loom that competes is broken by the weavers.

cards.subject: crown_town
cards.title: The mine at {town} floods
cards.text: Water broke into the deep shafts at {town}. The miners got out; the silver did not.

choices.label: Build pumps
text: Great wheels and pumps are raised at {town}.
At {town}, great wheels and pumps go up.
{town} raises pumps and great wheels at the mine.
The pumps clear the shafts; silver flows again.
The shafts are pumped dry, and the silver runs again.
Silver comes up once more from the drained shafts.

choices.label: Dig a new shaft higher up
text: A new shaft is begun.
Work starts on a new shaft.
A fresh shaft is begun, higher up.
The new shaft finds a thin vein.
The new shaft strikes a thin vein.
Only a thin vein waits in the new shaft.

choices.label: Close the mine
text: The miners of {town} look for other work.
{town}'s miners seek other work.
The miners of {town} go looking for new trades.
{town}'s miners drift away.
The miners of {town} drift off.
{town} loses its miners, one by one.

cards.subject: crown_town
cards.title: A toll bridge at {town}?
cards.text: {town}'s new bridge brings travellers. The steward says a penny a crossing would pay for it twice over.

choices.label: Toll it
text: Every traveller pays at {town}'s bridge.
At {town}'s bridge, every traveller pays.
No one crosses {town}'s bridge without paying.
Merchants find a ford upstream.
The merchants find a ford upriver.
Upstream, the merchants discover a ford.

choices.label: Keep it free
text: The bridge stays free; {town}'s market grows.
The bridge is free, and {town}'s market grows.
{town}'s market swells while the bridge costs nothing.
{town}'s market doubles; the crown's share grows with it.
{town}'s market doubles, and the crown's share with it.
The crown's share rises as {town}'s market doubles.

choices.label: Toll only foreigners
text: Foreign merchants pay; locals cross free.
Foreigners pay; locals cross free.
The toll falls on foreign merchants only.
{town} tolls the bridge itself, and keeps it.
{town} sets its own toll on the bridge, and keeps the coin.
The bridge toll is {town}'s, taken and kept.

cards.subject: realm
cards.title: Settlers want the empty lands
cards.text: Landless families ask leave to clear the wild country beyond the last royal town.

choices.label: Grant them land and tools
text: The families go out with axes and the King's blessing.
The families set out with axes and the King's blessing.
Axes in hand and blessed by the crown, the families go.
A new village thrives in the wild country, loyal to the crown.
In the wild country, a new village prospers, loyal to the crown.
The crown has a thriving new village in the wilds.

choices.label: Grant land, no tools
text: The families go with only their hands.
The families leave with nothing but their hands.
Empty-handed, the families set out.
Half the settlers come back hungry.
Half the settlers return, hungry.
Hungry, half of them come home.

choices.label: The wild country is the King's hunting ground
text: The families stay landless.
The families remain without land.
No land; the families wait.
The families go anyway, and owe the crown nothing.
The families go regardless, owing the crown nothing.
They go without leave, and owe the King nothing.

cards.subject: realm
cards.title: The sweating sickness
cards.text: A sickness that kills in a day is going through the towns. The lords are leaving for their country seats.

choices.label: Close the court
text: The court scatters; the King waits it out.
The court disperses, and the King sits it out.
With the court scattered, the King waits.
The sickness passes; the court returns, fewer.
The sickness passes, and a smaller court returns.
The court comes back when the sickness is gone, thinner.

choices.label: Stay at Kingsmere and be seen
text: The King stays; the realm notices.
The King remains, and the realm sees it.
The realm marks that the King stayed.
A dozen at court sicken; the King is spared.
A dozen at court fall sick; the King does not.
The sickness takes a dozen courtiers and spares the King.

choices.label: Pay physicians in every town
text: Physicians go out on the crown's silver.
The crown's silver sends physicians out.
Physicians ride to every town, paid by the crown.
The sickness runs its course through the realm.
The sickness takes its own course across the realm.
The realm is left to the sickness until it is done.

cards.subject: realm
cards.title: The lords want a jubilee
cards.text: The reign has been long. The great houses would celebrate it, and see what the King gives them.

choices.label: A jubilee for the realm
text: Bonfires burn on every hill for the King's long reign.
For the King's long reign, bonfires light every hill.
Every hilltop burns in honour of a long reign.

choices.label: A feast at Kingsmere
text: The lords feast; the towns don't.
The lords feast, and the towns go without.
A feast for the lords, and nothing for the towns.

choices.label: A reign is not a festival
text: The lords go home disappointed.
The lords leave for home, disappointed.
Disappointed, the lords go home.
The lords celebrate without the King.
The lords make merry without the King.
The celebrating is done by the lords alone.

cards.subject: realm
cards.title: The King's horse at the council table
cards.text: After a shouting match with the council, the King had his warhorse led into the hall and given the Steward's chair. The horse is still there. It has eaten the agenda.

choices.label: Leave the horse. It argues less
text: The horse keeps its chair. The lords learn to speak softly near it.
The horse stays on the council. Nobody dares move its chair.
The warhorse keeps the Steward's seat, and the lords keep their voices down.

choices.label: Give the Steward his chair back
text: The Steward sits again, smelling faintly of stable.
The Steward gets his chair back, and a fresh cushion.
The horse goes back to the stable. The Steward checks the chair before he sits.

choices.label: Make the horse a lord, with lands
text: Lord Hoof is granted a meadow by royal charter. The heralds are still drawing his arms.
The horse is made a lord with a meadow of his own. The great houses are not amused.
By charter, the horse holds a meadow and a title. Half the court laughs; the other half counts its own lands.
The horse stays where it is. Someone starts feeding it at meetings.
Nobody moves the horse. It becomes part of the council.
The horse keeps its seat by default. The minutes note its silence.

cards.subject: realm
cards.title: The King under the table
cards.text: A dropped tray in the great hall sounded like steel, and the King spent the rest of the feast under the high table. The lords saw. The lords always see.

choices.label: Say he was looking for his ring
text: Everyone agrees about the ring. Nobody believes it.
The story of the lost ring goes round. So does the true one.
The court nods at the tale of the ring, and smiles behind its cups.

choices.label: Laugh at himself, loudly
text: The King laughs first, and the hall laughs with him, not at him.
He makes the joke before anyone else can. It works.
The King toasts the tray that frightened him. The lords cheer.

choices.label: Ban trays from the hall
text: Trays are banned at court. The servants carry the food by hand, grimly.
No more trays in the hall, by order of the crown. The soup suffers most.
The decree goes up: no trays. The lords eat off their knees and talk of nothing else.
The tale grows with each telling. By winter there were three trays and a bear.
The story spreads unanswered and gets bigger.
Nobody answers it, so the taverns finish the story themselves.

cards.subject: crown_town
cards.title: A coin with the King's face, twice
cards.text: The mint at {town} has struck a new coin with the King's face on both sides, by his own order, so that nobody can ever toss it against him.

choices.label: Keep the coin. It is a fine face
text: The double-faced coin goes out. Merchants refuse it at the border.
The coin circulates. Gamblers hate it; the King loves it.
Every new coin shows the King twice. Trade at the border slows.

choices.label: Put the crown on the back instead
text: The back gets a crown, and the coin gets an honest chance again.
A crown goes on the reverse. The mint sighs with relief.
The coin is struck again with the crown on its back.

choices.label: Melt them and say nothing
text: The coins go back into the pot. The minters keep the secret.
The double coins are melted down quietly.
The mint melts the batch, and nobody speaks of it.
The coins go out as they are. Merchants start weighing them twice.
The double-faced coin spreads through the markets.
Nobody stops the mint. The coin is everywhere by harvest.

cards.subject: crown_town
cards.title: A fourth hand of the saint
cards.text: A friar at {town} offers the King a holy relic: the right hand of the realm's saint. The cathedral already holds three of them.

choices.label: Buy it. Faith is not arithmetic
text: The fourth hand is enshrined beside the other three. The friar leaves rich.
The King buys the hand. The bishops do not mention the count.
Four hands now rest in the cathedral. Pilgrims come to count them.

choices.label: Ask the friar how many hands a saint has
text: The friar says the saint was very generous. The King sends him away.
"A great saint," says the friar, "gave with many hands." He leaves with none of the King's gold.
The friar has an answer ready. The King is not buying it.

choices.label: Put the friar in the stocks at {town}
text: The friar spends a day in the stocks. The town throws turnips and laughs.
The friar is set in the stocks. The folk enjoy it more than any sermon.
A day in the stocks for the friar. The bishops look away.
The friar sells the hand to a lord instead. Now a great house has a saint's hand.
The relic finds another buyer in a great house.
Unbought by the King, the hand goes to a lord's chapel.

cards.subject: realm
cards.title: A bigger crown
cards.text: The King has asked the goldsmiths for a new crown, taller than the old one. The goldsmiths ask how tall. The King says: taller.

choices.label: Taller, then
text: The new crown is magnificent and heavy. The King's neck is stiff for a month.
A towering crown is made. Doorways become a matter of policy.
The goldsmiths deliver a crown so tall it has to be carried in on a cart.

choices.label: The old crown was good enough for his father
text: The old crown stays. The goldsmiths are paid for their trouble anyway.
He keeps his father's crown. It fits better than he admits.
The old crown stays on his head, and the gold stays in the chest.

choices.label: Have every lord pay for one jewel
text: Each great house sends a jewel. The crown is splendid; the houses keep the receipts.
The houses each pay for a stone. They will remember which one.
A jewel from every house goes into the crown. So does a little resentment.
The goldsmiths keep working, unsure when to stop.
Without an answer, the goldsmiths just keep adding gold.
Nobody tells the goldsmiths to stop. The bill grows.

cards.subject: crown_town
cards.title: The longest audience
cards.text: The King promised to hear every petitioner at {town} in person. On the ninth day of hearing them, the line is longer than when he started.

choices.label: Hear them all. He promised
text: He hears every last one. The folk of {town} speak of it for a generation.
Every petitioner is heard. It takes until the next season.
He does it. The last petitioner only wanted to see a King.

choices.label: Hear the first hundred, then feast
text: A hundred are heard, the rest are fed. Nobody complains much.
The first hundred get the King; the rest get bread and ale.
He listens to a hundred and feeds the rest. It works.

choices.label: Send the Steward in a spare crown
text: The Steward hears the rest in a borrowed crown. Some notice.
A Steward in a crown listens on. Half the line doesn't know the difference.
The Steward takes the chair in a spare crown. The folk are not fooled for long.
The line goes home on its own, slowly.
The petitioners give up and go home.
The line melts away with the weather.

cards.subject: realm
cards.title: The King challenges a bear
cards.text: Someone told the King that no man could beat the old bear of the royal forest. The King has sent for his sword.

choices.label: He goes. A King keeps his word
text: The King fights the bear and wins, barely. The bear becomes a rug and a legend.
He goes into the forest and comes out with the bear's head and a limp.
The bear loses. The King's scars are shown at every feast after.

choices.label: Send the bear a royal pardon instead
text: The bear is pardoned by charter. It does not read.
A herald nails a pardon to the bear's tree. The bear ignores it.
The bear receives the King's pardon and carries on as before.

choices.label: Fight it at a tourney, for show
text: The bear fights in the lists before every house. It is the tourney of the reign.
A tourney with a bear: the lords will never forget it.
The great houses come to watch the King and the bear. Everyone gets their story.
The bear lives, and the lords wonder about the King's courage.
Nobody fights the bear. The lords notice.
The bear is left alone, and so is the story.
